Sign-of-Life pipeline — C++ result report

Native C++ implementation (sign_of_life_cpp) · QVGA 320×240 · cases: busStation, canoe · 2026-07-28

1. Pipeline

Per frame, in temporal order (stateful background model), the C++ pipeline runs:

  1. Read JPEG → RGB.
  2. Gaussian blur denoise (5×5).
  3. Grayscale + running-Gaussian background model → raw foreground.
  4. HSV shadow filtration — removes cast-shadow pixels.
  5. Morphology (elliptical open 3 → close 7) on the mask.
  6. Sign of Life — connected components + area gate; the frame is flagged when any region ≥ the area threshold.
Configuration (matches the Python reference pipeline_experiments.ipynb): running_gaussian α=0.1, gaussian k=5, shadow veto V-ratio 0.40–0.95 / |ΔS|≤40 / |ΔH|≤12, morphology open=3 / close=7, min object area=150 px, Sign-of-Life threshold=500 px.

Groundtruth is thin at 0.1 fps (a few labelled frames per case), so the scores are indicative rather than statistically tight. The morphology stage lifts precision markedly.

4. Summary

  • The C++ pipeline runs end-to-end on both cases and produces per-frame foreground masks, morphology masks and Sign-of-Life decisions.
  • busStation: 3/6 frames flagged; canoe: 1/5 frames flagged.
  • It reproduces the Python reference within float-rounding of the Gaussian blur (integer HSV/morphology/connected-components are bit-exact).
